faqs.question: What do you say to someone whose birthday is on Halloween?
faqs.answer: Say happy birthday first, use their name, and add one Halloween touch at most, such as "The candy is for everyone else; the cake is for you." People born on 31 October often feel their day gets absorbed by costume parties, so a message that puts the birthday ahead of the holiday lands better.

faqs.question: Is it unlucky to be born on Halloween?
faqs.answer: No. There is no evidence that a birth date affects luck. In US records for 2000 to 2014, 31 October was simply less common than most dates, averaging 10,263 births a day against a daily mean of 11,350.

faqs.question: How many babies are born on 31 October each year?
faqs.answer: In the United States, an average of 10,263 babies were born on 31 October each year from 2000 to 2014, based on Social Security data published by FiveThirtyEight. In England and Wales the ONS figure for 1995 to 2014 is about 1,803, which is close to an ordinary day.

faqs.question: What should I write in a Halloween birthday card for a child?
faqs.answer: Keep it cute rather than scary: call them a little pumpkin or the friendliest ghost in town, mention their new age, and skip blood, monsters and jump-scare jokes. For children aged 3 to 10, one short sentence they can read themselves works better than a paragraph.

faqs.question: Should a Halloween birthday have its own separate party?
faqs.answer: Ask the birthday person. Many people born on 31 October like a separate day, or at least a separate cake moment, so the party is not just a Halloween night with candles. If the party is combined, sing happy birthday before the costume contest, not after.

faqs.question: What day of the week is Halloween in 2026 and 2027?
faqs.answer: Halloween falls on Saturday 31 October 2026 and Sunday 31 October 2027. A weekend birthday on Halloween means parties compete for the evening, so a morning message is the one most likely to be read.

faqs.question: Can a Halloween birthday page open exactly at midnight?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the premium Halloween page on SubhSandesh, which has an optional unlock time. Until that moment the link shows only the recipient's name and a countdown, so you can send it early and set it to open at 12:00 a.m. on their birthday.

faqs.question: What is a short happy birthday Halloween text?
faqs.answer: Try "Happy birthday! Your cake outranks every candy bowl tonight" or "Another year older, still the best treat on the street." Keep it under about 15 words so it reads fully in a phone notification.

faqs.question: How do I wish a coworker happy birthday on Halloween at work?
faqs.answer: Keep it light and work-safe, for example "Happy birthday! May your meetings vanish like ghosts." Avoid costume jokes about the person's appearance, and sign the team card before the office Halloween event takes over the afternoon.

faqs.question: Is 1 November too late for a Halloween birthday wish?
faqs.answer: No, a belated wish on 1 November is fine if you own the delay, for example "I got lost in the costume crowd. Belated happy birthday." Send it in the morning and skip the excuse paragraph; one honest line reads better than three.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Halloween Birthday Wishes for 31 October Birthdays and Beyond

The best Halloween birthday wishes say happy birthday first and Halloween second, because someone born on 31 October has watched their day vanish into costume parties for years. Below are 40 original lines sorted by whose birthday it is, from Halloween babies to spooky-themed parties in any month. Birthdays matter on SubhSandesh too: the birthday page for a partner is the #4 page type, with 510 created and 9.8% of all pages, and 48.3% of shared pages are opened on a phone.

So keep each line phone-sized. Further down: how rare a 31 October birthday is, which format suits whom, and when the theme backfires.

## What is a Halloween birthday wish?

A Halloween birthday wish is a birthday message that borrows Halloween imagery, such as pumpkins, ghosts, costumes or candy, because the birthday falls on or near 31 October or the party has a spooky theme. It names the person and the year ahead before it plays with the holiday.

It serves two groups: people born between 30 October and 1 November, and anyone throwing a spooky-themed birthday in another month. Halloween is a Saturday in 2026 and a Sunday in 2027, so weekend parties will compete with the cake.

## How rare is a 31 October birthday? US and UK birth data

In the United States, 31 October is one of the least common birthdays. I ran the [FiveThirtyEight's US daily births series, 2000 to 2014, from Social Security records](https://github.com/fivethirtyeight/data/tree/master/births), and 31 October averaged 10,263 births against a daily mean of 11,350, ranking 355th of the 365 regular dates.

The dip belongs to the day itself. Against the same weekday a week before and a week after, 31 October ran 11.8% lower across those 15 years, while 30 October ran 2.6% lower and 1 November 1.8% higher. Still, about 153,900 Americans born then share Halloween as a birthday.

England and Wales show no dip. The [Office for National Statistics birthday popularity data for 1995 to 2014](https://www.ons.gov.uk/peoplepopulationandcommunity/birthsdeathsandmarriages/livebirths/articles/howpopularisyourbirthday/2015-12-18), published 18 December 2015, gives 31 October an average of 1,803 births a day against a 1,813 mean, 197th of 365 by my count. Neither dataset explains the US drop, though [Macfarlane and Dattani's 2019 linked-records analysis](https://ijpds.org/article/view/1296) found planned caesareans clustered into weekday mornings, so hospital timetables do move birth dates.

## 40 Halloween birthday wishes, sorted by whose birthday it is

Each group names who it suits and the tone. Add their name or age so the line reads as written for them.

### 1. Born on 31 October

For the friend or relative whose birthday has always shared a date with Halloween. Affectionate and a little defiant on their behalf, 7 lines.

- Happy birthday to the one guest at tonight's party who didn't need a costume to be the main event.
- You showed up on the darkest, silliest night of the calendar and have kept things lively ever since. Happy birthday.
- Every porch on the street lights up for you tonight. I've decided that's on purpose.
- The candy is for everyone else; the cake is for you. Happy birthday.
- Born on Halloween, which explains the magic and absolutely nothing else. Have a wonderful birthday.
- Today the whole world dresses up for your birthday and pretends it's for something else.
- Happy birthday! Your candles and the carved pumpkins outside can fight over who glows brightest.

### 2. Born on 30 October or 1 November

For near-miss birthdays, where the person is tired of hearing "so close to Halloween". Playful about the closeness, 5 lines.

- Happy eve-of-Halloween birthday. You get the quiet before the chaos, all to yourself.
- Happy birthday on the day the costumes go back in the cupboard. You're the reason November starts well.
- The leftover candy is all yours, birthday rules. Have a brilliant 1 November.
- Close enough to Halloween to get the decorations, far enough to keep the spotlight. Happy birthday.
- The ghosts have gone home and you're still here, shining. Happy birthday.

### 3. A Halloween-themed party in any month

For a birthday someone chose to theme spooky, whatever the month. Party-ready and short enough for a gift tag, 6 lines.

- Halloween in May? Only for you. Happy birthday, and I'm bringing my best cape.
- Thank you for a birthday where the dress code is "monster" and I finally fit in.
- Happy birthday to the host brave enough to hang cobwebs in summer.
- Another year older, another year spookier. I'm dying to know what you're dressing as.
- May your birthday bring a full bowl of sweets, a few good scares and nobody stepping on your cape.
- See you at the haunted party. I'll be the ghost carrying your present.

### 4. Kids turning a year older in costume

For children from about 3 to 10, read aloud or written in a card. Cute rather than scary, no blood or monsters, 6 lines.

- Happy birthday, little pumpkin! You're one whole year bigger and twice as brave.
- The friendliest ghost in town is having a birthday, and it's you.
- You're seven now: old enough to choose your own costume, young enough to wear it all week.
- Happy birthday to our favourite tiny witch. May your wand work on every candle.
- Boo! That was the birthday surprise. The real one is downstairs.
- One more year of growing, giggling and trick-or-treating. Happy birthday, sweetheart.

### 5. A partner with a Halloween birthday

For a girlfriend, boyfriend, husband or wife, as a pillow card or morning text. Warm with one spooky wink, 6 lines.

- Happy birthday to the person I'd happily haunt forever.
- Of all the treats tonight, you're still the one I'd choose first.
- I married into a lifetime of birthday cake and fun-size candy, and I'm not complaining.
- You make every 31 October the best night of my year, and it has nothing to do with costumes.
- Happy birthday, love. I'll wear the matching costume if you wear the birthday crown.
- Another year of you, which beats anything in the candy bowl.

### 6. A friend or coworker

For a team card, a group chat or someone you like but don't see daily. Light and safe for work, 5 lines.

- Happy birthday! Hope the office candy bowl is officially renamed in your honour.
- Wishing you a spooky-good birthday and a desk free of fake spiders.
- Happy birthday from all of us. Today's costume theme is "pretending we remembered the cake".
- Happy Halloween birthday! May your meetings vanish like ghosts.
- Cheers to another year of you making work less scary.

### 7. Late or belated wishes

For anyone who missed the day, usually because Halloween ate the evening. Apologetic and honest, 5 lines.

- I got lost in the costume crowd. Belated happy birthday, and I owe you cake.
- The decorations are down but my wishes aren't. Happy belated birthday.
- My memory played a trick on me; please accept this late treat. Happy birthday.
- A day late and a candy bar short. Happy belated birthday, friend.
- Halloween distracted me, but you're worth remembering all month. Happy belated birthday.

## How to keep the birthday from vanishing into Halloween

Send the wish before 10 a.m., on its own rather than inside a group Halloween message. Evenings fill fast on a weekend Halloween, and a morning message gets read before the party noise.

Use one Halloween reference per wish. Two puns turn it into a seasonal greeting with a name attached.

Families protect birthday gatherings even under pressure: a [2026 JAMA Network Open cohort study of 1,106,493 grandparents in Denmark](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13366199) found a 9.9% higher hazard of SARS-CoV-2 infection in the week after a grandchild's birthday, despite periods of official advice not to gather. A birthday sharing its date with a bigger holiday deserves that loyalty too.

## Which format suits a Halloween birthday wish? 4 options compared

Four ways to send the lines above. Values reflect what each format holds.

| Format | Time to make | Photos | Best for |
|---|---|---|---|
| Text message | Under 1 minute | 0–1 attached | Coworkers, group chats, belated wishes |
| Handwritten card | 10–15 minutes plus delivery | 0 | Grandparents, kids who keep cards |
| Interactive Halloween card page | About 5 minutes | Up to 6 | A friend, sibling or child born on 31 October |
| Premium Halloween page | About 10 minutes | Up to 12, plus a 60-second voice note | A partner whose birthday is Halloween |

A text wins on speed; a page wins when the birthday deserves more. Each created SubhSandesh page averages 11.1 views.

## Sending the wish as a Halloween birthday page

Neither Halloween template has a birthday mode, so the birthday lives in your letter and photos. For a playful card, the [interactive Halloween card with photos and music](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween) needs roughly five minutes and up to 6 photos and its closing question (60 characters maximum) can become a birthday one. The Boo License says "Valid every 31 October, forever", which lands differently when that date is their birthday.

For a partner, the [premium Halloween page with a voice note and unlock time](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween-premium) needs roughly ten minutes and holds 12 photos, a 60-second voice note and a 3,000-character letter. Set its unlock time to midnight on their birthday, so until then they see just their name and a countdown, and they can answer once through the reply box.

For a birthday unrelated to Halloween, a [birthday surprise page for a partner](https://subhsandesh.in/birthday-gf) fits better, and [the full template gallery](https://subhsandesh.in/templates) covers friends and family on other dates. 38.5% of creators password-protect their page before sharing it, an option on both Halloween templates.

## When a Halloween birthday wish is the wrong choice

Some 31 October people dislike the theme after decades of costume-party birthdays. If they have ever said "it's my birthday, not Halloween", send a plain birthday message and leave the pumpkins out.

It also misfires for anyone who skips Halloween on religious grounds, a child scared of ghosts, or someone grieving near All Souls' Day on 2 November. For a relative without a phone or laptop, a posted card beats any link, and both templates are English-only, one-person pages that cannot invite a crowd.

## Sources

- FiveThirtyEight, US births 2000–2014 (SSA data), GitHub, undated.
- Office for National Statistics, "How popular is your birthday?", 18 December 2015.
- Macfarlane and Dattani, International Journal of Population Data Science, 22 November 2019.
- Espenhain et al., JAMA Network Open, 1 July 2026.

auditReport.honestAssessment: An answer engine has a reason to cite this page for the 31 October birth-date question: no ranking page measures how rare a Halloween birthday is, and this one gives the US 355th-of-365 rank and the UK no-dip contrast from public birth records, plus 40 original lines sorted by whose birthday it is rather than one generic block. The SERP is weak (6 of 9 results spam, stale or year-stamped), but aol.com and scoopwhoop.com carry far more authority, the US birth series ends in 2014, and no first-party Halloween usage data exists, so expect months, not weeks.
